title: ksTable Table Specification v1
description: Declarative JSON DSL for ksTable — a pure-R generator that compiles table specifications into human-readable dplyr/tidyr scripts. The generated script is evaluated against a user-supplied data frame; calc and format functions are resolved by name from the evaluation environment.

schema_version.description: Schema version string. Should be '1.0' for this schema.

r_identifier.description: A valid R identifier: must start with a letter or a dot, followed by zero or more letters, digits, dots, or underscores. This constraint is enforced for security (SR-1 injection prevention): values that do not match cannot be safely embedded in generated R code.

table_spec.description: Root table specification. Defines what to compute (statistics over parameters), how to group the data (groups), and how to arrange the output (layout).

id.description: Optional unique identifier for this table, used for caching and cross-references.

title.description: Optional human-readable title, passed to ksTFL for use in rendered output headers.

parameter.description: Named map of parameters. Each key is a parameter identifier (used internally); each value defines a variable in the input data frame. For parameter_stat layout, each parameter produces one block of rows. For hierarchical layout, exactly one parameter with a nested child is expected.

statistics.description: Named map of statistics. Each key is a statistic identifier; each value defines how to compute and display one statistic. The order of keys determines the row order in the output.

parameter.description: A parameter binds a display label to one or more columns in the input data frame. Use 'variable' for a single column or 'variables' for an array of columns sharing the same statistics (each expands into its own row block).

variable.description: Single column name. Mutually exclusive with 'variables'.

variables.description: Array of column names, each producing its own row block. Use with 'labels' to assign display names. Mutually exclusive with 'variable'.

labels.description: Display labels corresponding to each entry in 'variables'. If shorter than 'variables', missing labels default to the variable name.

label.description: Display label when using 'variable' (singular). Defaults to the variable name if omitted.

nested.description: One child parameter for the 'hierarchical' row structure.

nested_parameter.description: Child parameter for hierarchical tables (e.g. Preferred Term under System Organ Class). The child variable produces the .row_label in child rows (.is_child = TRUE).

variable.description: Child column name in the input data frame, e.g. 'AEDECOD'. Must be a valid R identifier (SR-1).

label.description: Optional display label for child rows. Rarely used since .row_label already holds the child variable value.

statistic.description: One cell value in the output table. The compiler generates a dplyr::summarize() + dplyr::mutate() pair for each statistic. The compute step stores the raw value in .value_raw; the format step converts it to a display string in .value.

fun.description: Name of the calc function resolved from the evaluation environment. Receives the analysis column for one group as the first argument. When 'denominator' is set, the compiler also passes denom = <resolved scalar>. May return a scalar or a named list (e.g. list(n=..., pct=...)). Must be a valid R identifier (SR-1).

apply_to.description: Optional allow-list controlling which parameters this statistic applies to. Each entry can be a parameter ID (e.g. 'cont') or a variable name (e.g. 'AGE'). If omitted, the statistic applies to all parameters.

denominator_spec.description: Declares how the compiler resolves the scalar 'denom' argument passed to fun(variable, denom = ...). The calc function owns percent math; the DSL only wires the denominator.

type.description:
Denominator kind.

'n': rows in the current groups.by cell (dplyr::n()).

'n_distinct': distinct values of 'variable' in the current cell.

'data_n': pre-aggregate analysis data over a subset of groups.by (optional distinct), join back, use dplyr::first(.kst_dK).

'external': object from the evaluation environment (population / big-N). With 'by', join/lookup keyed columns; without 'by', treat as a scalar symbol.

variable.description: For type 'n_distinct': column whose distinct count is the denominator.

by.description: For 'data_n' and 'external': key columns used to aggregate or look up N. Must be a subset of groups.by.

distinct.description: For type 'data_n': optional column for n_distinct during pre-aggregation. If omitted, row count (dplyr::n()) is used.

name.description: For type 'external': name of the object in the evaluation environment (tibble or scalar).

value.description: For type 'external' with a tibble: column holding N. Ignored for scalar externals.

function_args.description: Extra named arguments appended to the fun(variable, ...) call in the generated script. Example: {"na.rm": true, "probs": 0.25} generates ', na.rm = TRUE, probs = 0.25'. Keys must be valid R identifiers (SR-1). Values are serialised to R literals: JSON true/false → R TRUE/FALSE; JSON null → R NULL; numbers and strings → corresponding R literals.

additionalProperties.description: Argument value. Supported JSON types: boolean, number, string, null.

format_spec.description: Specification for converting the raw .value_raw to the display string .value. Every statistic has a formatter; when this field is omitted the default formatter is as.character(). All formatters must return a single character string per group.

type.description:
Format type. Each type emits a different R expression in the generated script.

'sprintf': scalar numeric → sprintf(pattern, .value_raw). The calc function must return a scalar.

'custom': named-list → vapply(.value_raw, fun, character(1L)). The calc function must return a named list; the format function receives one list element and returns a character string.

'template': named-list → vapply(.value_raw, function(.x) glue::glue_data(.x, pattern), character(1L)). Like 'custom' but uses a glue template string instead of a function.

'ksformat': any → ksformat::fput(.value_raw, format_name). Applies a registered ksformat VALUE format.

pattern.description: For type 'sprintf': a printf-style format string, e.g. '%.1f' or '%.0f%%'. For type 'template': a glue template string with named placeholders matching the keys of the named list returned by the calc function, e.g. '{mean} ({sd})' or '{n} ({pct}%)'.

fun.description: For type 'custom': name of the format function in the evaluation environment. Must accept the named list returned by the calc function and return a single character string. Must be a valid R identifier (SR-1).

format_name.description: For type 'ksformat': the name of a VALUE format registered in the ksformat package, e.g. 'trt_fmt'.

groups.description: Stratification specification. The 'by' columns determine the output column headers after pivot_wider.

by.description: Ordered array of column names to group by. The unique combinations of values in these columns become the column headers of the output tibble. Each entry must be a valid R identifier (SR-1).

items.description: Column name. Must be a valid R identifier.

include_missing_levels.description: When true, the generator emits group_by(..., .drop = FALSE) so that factor levels with zero observations in a group still appear as rows (with the default formatter's value, e.g. '0'). Requires the grouping columns to be factors with the complete set of levels before evaluating compiled code. Use kst_apply_metadata() to ensure correct factor levels.

format.description: Optional documentation map from a grouping column name to a ksformat VALUE format name. Not applied by kst_compile(). Pass the same mapping as format_map to kst_extract_metadata() / kst_apply_metadata() before evaluating generated code so group headers use display labels and include_missing_levels works.

layout.description: Controls how rows and columns are organised in the output tibble.

row_structure.description:
Row organisation strategy.

'parameter_stat' (default): one output row per parameter × statistic combination. The output tibble has columns .param (parameter label) and .stat (statistic key) as row identifiers.

'hierarchical': parent rows followed by child rows nested beneath each parent, sorted alphabetically within each parent. Requires exactly one top-level parameter with exactly one nested child. The output tibble has columns .parent, .is_child (FALSE = parent row, TRUE = child row), .row_label, and .stat (statistic key) as row identifiers. The .parent and .is_child columns are consumed by ksTFL to apply indentation and group headers.

column_structure.description: Column organisation strategy. Currently only 'groups' is supported: each unique combination of the groups.by values becomes a separate output column. Column ordering follows first-appearance order in the data; use factor levels via kst_apply_metadata() to control ordering.
